summary.name: Qodo
summary.one_liner: Qodo is an AI code review and governance platform that reviews pull requests with cross-repo codebase context, enforces coding standards, and oversees AI coding tools and agents.
use_cases: Automated first-pass review of pull requests
Enforcing team coding standards across repos
Catching breaking changes in shared libraries or APIs across repos
Real-time code validation inside the IDE
Governing AI coding tool skill files in an enterprise
summary.what_it_does: Qodo reviews every pull request using context from across the codebase, not just the diff, and flags bugs, rule violations, duplicated logic, and ticket or requirement gaps with severity levels. It can mine rules automatically from recurring PR comments and reviewer decisions, and tracks how often rules are violated and resolved before merge. Its Cross Repo Review maps dependencies between repos and can flag signature changes that would break downstream consumers, including across GitHub and GitLab. The same rules and review agents run in the IDE (VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio) and on Git pull requests.
notable: Cross Repo Review flags breaking changes in shared SDKs, APIs, or schemas before merge, including across Git providers
Rules Miner turns PR comments and reviewer decisions into enforceable coding rules
SOC 2 Type II certified, zero data retention, and BYOK support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, or self-hosted models
Skill Review Standards give analytics and enable/disable controls for AI tool skill files
caveats: Pro Team plan is credit-based at $0.012 per credit (e.g. 2,500 credits for about 18 reviews/month), and a 14-day free trial is offered
Enterprise plans with SSO/SAML, BYOK, single-tenant or on-prem deployment and priority support are on a separate pricing tier
Review-count figures and time-saved claims (~1 hour per PR, 90% of initial review) are vendor-stated
